Sauté the chicken in olive oil in a pot: Add the leek and carrot and stir for 5 minutes.
Add the hot water, salt and pepper; cook covered over low heat for 12 minutes.
Whisk the lemon juice with the flour until smooth, add to the dish and simmer for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Sprinkle with chopped dill and serve.
The lemon and flour mixture lightly thickens the sauce and acts like a liaison.
Serve with rice pilaf and yogurt.
Chicken with tomato and basil
4 boneless chicken thighs (about 500 g)
A handful of fresh basil (or 1 teaspoon dried)
A pinch of sugar
Rub the chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and cook the thighs for a total of 8 minutes until golden on both sides, then transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, fry the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato, sugar and half the basil and cook for 5 minutes.
Place the chicken in the sauce and cook covered over low heat for 12 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C.
Sprinkle with the remaining fresh basil and serve.
Thigh stays juicier than breast; if using breast, cut the time by 3–4 minutes.
Serve with pasta, mashed potatoes or bulgur.
Chicken with ginger and carrots
400 g chicken breast (thin strips)
2 carrots (julienned)
1 dessert spoon starch
2 tablespoons sunflower oil
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, starch and 3 tablespoons of water in a bowl to make the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wide pan or wok over very high heat; cook the chicken for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, and transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, sauté the carrot and pepper for 3 minutes, keeping them crisp.
Add the ginger, garlic and white parts of the spring onions and stir for 1 minute.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and stir for 1–2 minutes until glossy and thick.
Serve with the green parts of the spring onions and sesame seeds.
For wok dishes, prepare all the ingredients in advance; cooking is very fast.
Serve with plain rice pilaf.
Baked sea bass with lemon and dill
2 sea bass fillets (about 350 g in total)
A quarter teaspoon black pepper
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and lightly grease a small baking dish.
Finely chop half the dill; mix with olive oil, garlic, thyme, grated lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Pat the fillets dry, place skin side down in the dish and spread the dill mixture over them.
Place thin lemon slices and a small knob of butter on each fillet.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes with a fork.
Serve drizzled with the remaining fresh dill and the juices from the dish.
Sea bass fillets are thin, so don’t go beyond 15 minutes.
The lemon slices keep the top of the fish moist.
Serve with steamed vegetables or rice pilaf.
Eat the same day; keep for no more than 1 day in the fridge.
Baked salmon with orange and fennel
2 salmon fillets (about 150 g each)
1 fennel (thinly sliced)
1 orange (half sliced, half juiced)
1 small red onion (thinly sliced)
1 teaspoon mustard
Toss the fennel and onion slices with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and a pinch of salt, spread in a baking dish and pre-bake for 10 minutes.
Whisk the orange juice, honey, mustard, remaining olive oil, salt and pepper.
Place the salmon on the fennel, brush with half the sauce and tuck the orange slices in between.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the salmon reaches an internal temperature of 63 °C.
Drizzle the remaining sauce over when serving.
Don’t throw away the green fennel fronds; sprinkle them over when serving.
If mustard isn’t liked, it can be left out; the taste will be sweeter.
Serve with quinoa or bulgur pilaf.
Baked sea bream with leeks
2 sea bream fillets
2 leeks (2 cm rings)
1 carrot (thin rounds)
Wash the leek rings in plenty of water and clean out the grit.
Sauté the leek, carrot and garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil for 5 minutes; add the hot water and half a teaspoon of salt and cook covered for 8 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C; spread the leek mixture in a baking dish.
Season the bream fillets with salt and pepper, place on the leeks and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Bake for 15 minutes until the fish turns white.
Squeeze lemon over and serve hot.
Pre-cooking the leeks lets them soften without drying out the fish.
Serve with the leeks from the dish and yogurt on the side.
Keep for 1 day in the fridge.
Baked fish with mushrooms and thyme
4 sea bass or sea bream fillets
Slice the mushrooms, slice the onion thinly and cut the tomato into rounds.
Toss the vegetables with olive oil, thyme and half the salt, spread on a tray and pre-bake for 10 minutes.
Arrange the fish on the vegetables and add the remaining salt and lemon juice.
Bake for 15 minutes until the fish is opaque.
The fillets are thin, so don’t overcook them; they dry out.
With rocket and lemon.
Baked pear and walnut dessert
3 tablespoons coarsely chopped walnuts
2 tablespoons oat flour
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Peel and dice the pears; coarsely chop the walnuts.
Whisk the milk, oat flour and cinnamon in a separate bowl; add to the fruit mixture.
Divide the mixture evenly among small baking dishes and smooth the tops with a spoon.
Bake on the middle rack for about 25-30 minutes until set; serve lukewarm.
Baked pumpkin and walnut dessert
300 g pumpkin
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Dice the pumpkin small and steam for 12 minutes until soft.
Baked plum and oat dessert
8 plums
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Pit the plums, quarter them and toss with the oats.
Baked apricot and almond dessert
8 apricots
3 tablespoons flaked almonds
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Halve the apricots and remove the stones; set the almonds aside.
Baked sour cherry and oat dessert
1 cup pitted sour cherries
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Pit the sour cherries and mix with the oats.
Baked date and cocoa dessert
6 pitted dates
1 tablespoon cocoa
Preheat the oven to 180°C; wash, pit and chop the fruit.
Mix the main ingredients with the milk, oat flour and cinnamon.
Divide the mixture among small baking dishes and smooth the tops.
Bake for about 20-30 minutes until lightly golden on top and hot inside; serve lukewarm.
Pasta with spinach and lor cheese
350 g penne pasta
150 g lor
1 dessert spoon salt, half a teaspoon black pepper, a pinch of nutmeg
Boil the pasta in salted water and reserve 1 cup of the cooking water.
Stir the garlic in oil for 1 minute.
Add the spinach and let it wilt for 2 minutes.
Make a creamy sauce with the lor and a little cooking water.
Add the pasta and mix.
Nutmeg brings out the flavour of spinach.
Serve hot as soon as it’s cooked.

350 g penne
